name: HAWC water-Cherenkov array
notes: The tank count (commonly cited elsewhere as 300) is not recorded: no source consulted states it (the design paper's text could not be extracted and the official site was unreachable). A technical source that states it would settle it.

altitude.quote: under construction 4100 meters above sea level at Sierra Negra, Mexico

summary.plain: An array of closed water tanks on a Mexican volcano that sense the faint flashes of light left by particles from gamma-ray and cosmic-ray showers as they pass through the water.
summary.technical: Water-Cherenkov extensive-air-shower array at 4100 m on Sierra Negra, Mexico; full-array operations since March 2015. Tank count and individual tank dimensions are not recorded (the source papers with those specifications could not be read).

technology.note: Named for its detection technique; exact tank count and geometry are not sourced (see notes).
technology.value: Array of closed water-Cherenkov detector tanks continuously sampling extensive air showers from gamma rays and cosmic rays.
